columns.name: socio
columns.label: Socioeconomic classification, 1994-2001 version
columns.note: Uses socio13's lookup, but the two do not agree on code 111. columns.name: famaekvivadisp_13
columns.label: Household-equivalised disposable income
columns.note: This is the family's disposable income divided by an equivalence factor, so that families of different sizes can be compared. The factor counts the first adult as 1.0, each further person over 14 as 0.5, and each child under 15 as 0.3: a couple with two young children comes to 1 + 0.5 + 0.6 = 2.1, so a family income of 420,000 is recorded as 200,000 for each of the four. `FAMDISPONIBEL_13` is the same money before that division, and `FAMAEKVIVAINDKNETTO` is a different income concept (total income with net interest), so check which one your analysis plan means. The `_13` suffix marks the definition that replaced the older variables from 2013: DST states that FAMDISPONIBEL was discontinued in 2013 and replaced by FAMDISPONIBEL_13. A study spanning 2013 has to know which side of that change it is on. DST's year ranges settle the relationship with the sister column FAMAEKVIVADISP, which has no _13: the old one runs 1990-2012, this one runs 1987-2024. The _13 definition was applied backwards as well as forwards, so it is not a newer variable covering later years only. A study spanning the 2013 changeover should use _13 for the whole period rather than splicing the two, which would mix two definitions in one series.
columns.derivation: FAMAEKVIVADISP_13 = FAMDISPONIBEL_13 / (1 + (0.5 * (number of people over 14 in the family - 1)) + (0.3 * number of people under 15 in the family))

columns.name: year

columns.name: famaekvivadisp
columns.label: Equivalised disposable family income
columns.note: The same weighting scheme as FAMAEKVIVADISP_13 below, just algebraically rearranged on the source page: the first adult over 14 counts as 1.0, each further person over 14 as 0.5, and each child under 15 as 0.3. All persons belonging to the same family on 31 December of the income year (same E-familienummer), including resident children under 25, are assigned the family's equivalised income. `FAMDISPONIBEL` is the same money before that division.
columns.derivation: FAMAEKVIVADISP = FAMDISPONIBEL / (0.5 + (0.5 * number of people over 14 in the family) + (0.3 * number of people under 15 in the family))

columns.name: famaekvivaindknetto
columns.label: Equivalised total income including net interest
columns.derivation: FAMAEKVIVAINDKNETTO = FAMSUMINDKNETTORENT / (0.5 + (0.5 * number of people over 14 in the family) + (0.3 * number of people under 15 in the family))

columns.note: The key to lpr_a_kontakt, which is where pnr lives. This table carries no person identifier of its own.

columns.name: proc_starttidspunkt
columns.label: Procedure start
columns.note: A datetime, not a date. as.Date() it before comparing with an index date.

columns.name: proc_kode_type
columns.label: Procedure code type
columns.note: "P" marks a procedure, "+" an add-on code. An add-on code modifies the procedure above it and is not a procedure in its own right, so counting all rows overcounts.

columns.name: proc_parent_kode
columns.label: Parent procedure code
columns.note: LPR3 nests procedures the same way it nests diagnoses: an add-on code points at the procedure it belongs to.

columns.name: dw_ek_forloeb
columns.label: Course identifier
columns.note: One level above the contact. Where dw_ek_kontakt is empty, this is the only route back to a person, and it reaches a whole course of treatment rather than a single contact.

columns.name: flag_proc_uden_kont
columns.label: Procedure without a contact
columns.note: Flags a procedure with no contact attached. Those rows cannot be joined to lpr_a_kontakt at all, so a plain inner join drops them silently.

columns.name: lprindberetningssystem
columns.label: Reporting system
columns.note: Filter to "LPR3" when combining with LPR2, or contacts reported under both systems are counted twice.

columns.name: proc_indb_tidspunkt
columns.label: Reporting time
columns.note: When the procedure was reported, not when it happened. Recent months look incomplete because reporting lags.

columns.name: recnum
columns.label: Contact identifier
columns.note: The key every other LPR2 dataset joins on. It identifies a contact, not a person.

columns.name: d_inddto
columns.label: Date of admission
columns.note: Use this as the contact date. It is the admission date, so for an outpatient course it is the date the course started, not the date of a particular visit.

columns.name: c_spec
columns.label: Specialty
columns.note: DST publishes what each specialty code means in its department and specialty overview: https://www.dst.dk/da/Statistik/dokumentation/Times/moduldata-for-sociale-forhold--sundhedsvaesen--retsvaesen/spec (in Danish). The codes are not self-explanatory, so look them up rather than grouping on the digits.

columns.name: c_adiag

columns.name: v_alder

columns.name: c_indm
columns.label: Admission mode
columns.note: Used together with c_pattype to separate emergency-room contacts from ordinary outpatient ones after about 2014, see the LPR extraction chapter. Available for the register's whole span, so a missing c_indm is an extract boundary rather than a coverage gap.

columns.name: c_udm

columns.name: c_bopamt

atc.name: ATC (Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical)
atc.description: The WHO classification of medicines. Five cumulative levels: 1 character (anatomical main group), 3 (therapeutic subgroup), 4 (pharmacological subgroup), 5 (chemical subgroup), 7 (chemical substance). Each level repeats the levels above it and adds characters, so C09AA05 contains C, C09, C09A and C09AA.
atc.note: As a rule, filter on the full 7-character code rather than on the level columns: `atc2` holds three characters, so a longer pattern matched against it can never match, and it returns nothing at all with no error. The level columns are well suited to grouping, and to filtering when every code you want is the same length as the column.

beskst.name: Beskaeftigelsesstatus, 1976-2001 (AKM/Indkomst)
beskst.description: A person's main labour-market position during the year: self-employed, an employee, a pensioner, or one of a few other categories. The predecessor to beskst02, with a shorter, coarser code list.
beskst.note: Not comparable with beskst02, in DST's own words, not just a difference of degree: people with an unemployment share over 50 percent, and people on efterløn (early retirement pay), get their own codes under beskst02 that this code list does not have, and the rules for who counts as self-employed also changed. See beskst02's reader_note.

beskst02.name: Beskaeftigelsesstatus, 2002 onwards (AKM/Indkomst)
beskst02.description: A person's main labour-market position during the year. Longer and finer than the 1976-2001 predecessor (beskst): it splits out efterløn, dagpenge and kontanthjælp recipients as their own categories instead of folding them into broader ones. Shared by beskst02 and beskst13, which use the same codes.
beskst02.note: Not comparable with beskst (see beskst's own reader_note): DST states this directly, not just a difference of degree. Comparable with beskst13 with named exceptions: self-employment income is measured net of capital income in beskst13 rather than gross, and beskst13's amount thresholds are price-adjusted where beskst02's are not. A study spanning both should read DST's own change note before treating them as one continuous series.

c_dodsmaade.name: Doedsmaade, to 2001 (DAR t_dodsaarsag_1)
c_dodsmaade.description: How the person died, as coded in the FIRST cause-of-death table, which is what dodsaars holds. The set was reorganised on 1 January 1991, and the lookup below is the one in force from that date. A second, different set of numbers is used from 2002: see `c_dodsmaade_2002`.
c_dodsmaade.note: Two separate traps. First, this code set is NOT the one used from 2002: in dodsaasg the same column holds `c_dodsmaade_2002`, where 1 is Voldshandling rather than Naturlig død. Second, code 4 changed meaning. It was Selvmord until 31 December 1990 and Drab/vold from 1 January 1991. dodsaars runs from 1970 to 2001 and so contains both, in one column, with nothing to tell them apart except the date of death. Reading code 4 as one thing across the whole register counts homicides as suicides or the reverse. Codes 6 (Drab/vold) and 9 (Uoplyst) belong only to the old set and stop at the end of 1990; codes 3 and 5 only start in 1991.

c_dodsmaade_2002.name: Doedsmaade, 2002 onwards (DAR t_dodsaarsag_2)
c_dodsmaade_2002.description: How the person died, as coded from 2002. A different set of numbers from the one used until 2001, for the same five concepts. Nothing marks the change in the data itself: the column has the same name in both registers.
c_dodsmaade_2002.note: This is the set behind the `c_dodsmaade` column in dodsaasg, and the numbers do not mean what the same numbers mean in `dodsaars`. There, under `c_dodsmaade`, 1 is Naturlig død, 2 is Ulykke and 5 is Uoplyst. Here 1 is Voldshandling, 2 is Selvmord and 5 is Naturlig død. A study that spans 2001 and 2002 is reading two different code sets out of two columns with the same name, and every value maps to something plausible in the other set, so nothing looks wrong. A blank is a registration error, not a missing manner of death.

diagtype.name: Diagnosetype (LPR2 c_diagtype)
diagtype.description: Whether a diagnosis is the reason for the contact, an additional condition, or something else. Six codes, three of which were discontinued.
diagtype.note: The guide long described this as an A/B/G column. There are six codes, and three of them stop: **G runs 1995-2003 only**, M 1998-2013 and C 2002-2013. A and B run the whole period, H from 1995. So a comorbidity definition built on G silently covers nine years and nothing else, and filtering to A/B/G drops referral diagnoses entirely. Which types to keep is a case definition, not a technicality: outcomes usually use A and B. Carry the type column into the extract so the definition can be varied later.

disco_old.name: DISCO fagklassifikation, foer 2010
disco_old.description: Occupation code before the 2010 switch to DISCO-08. Shares the general shape of DISCO-08 (a hierarchical numeric code) but not its published value list: DST's nomenklaturer page for "disco" now serves DISCO-08 itself, and no archived version of the pre-2010 code list has been found.
disco_old.note: Do not read a code here against DISCO-08's published list (disco08.yaml): the two classifications share the general numeric shape but DST revised the detail at the 2010 switch, and a code that means one occupation in DISCO-08 is not guaranteed to mean the same thing, or to exist at all, in the pre-2010 scheme.

disco08.name: DISCO-08 fagklassifikation (occupation)
disco08.description: Danmarks Statistiks Fagklassifikation (DISCO-08), the occupation classification current from 2010. Hierarchical: level 1 is 10 broad groups, level 5 the full six-digit code.
disco08.note: The AKM columns do not draw purely from this file. Checked against disco08_alle_indk's own value list on DST's high-quality variable page: only 564 of its 790 distinct codes appear in this CSV's 564 level-5 codes. disco_typ (see discotyp.yaml) explains why: the occupation code for a given person-year can come from several source registers of varying vintage and quality, including imputation, so a study will see codes this file's current edition does not carry. Do not treat a code missing from this CSV as an error in the data before checking discotyp.

discotyp.name: Kilde til DISCO-koden (AKM)
discotyp.description: Which source register supplied a person's DISCO occupation code, and how it was obtained: reported directly, carried over from the year before, or imputed. Not the occupation itself, only where that code came from, which matters because DST states code quality is best when this is 1, 2, 4 or 10, and worse for the other, imputation-based values.
discotyp.note: A different question from the DISCO occupation code itself: this says where that code came from, not what the job was. DST's own page states that DISCO code quality is best when discotyp is 1, 2, 4 or 10, and that the remaining codes mean the DISCO code was set by imputation.

herkomst.note: A descendant is born in Denmark: neither parent is both a Danish citizen and born in Denmark. So the category says something about the parents, not about where the person was born, and it does not change over a lifetime the way citizenship does.

hfaudd.name: DISCED-15 AUDD (completed education)
hfaudd.description: The code for a completed education under DISCED-15. Four digits identifying which education, not how long or how high it is. DISCED-15 has a separate code for an ongoing or interrupted education (UDD).
hfaudd.note: This is an identifier, not a scale. The level (short, medium, long) has to be looked up in a separate table, and cannot be read off the digits: 4112 is an electrician, and taking the first two digits as a level code makes it a long higher education. DST documents the ongoing-education codes separately as DISCED-15 UDD.

hustype.name: Husstandstype
hustype.description: The type of household a person lives in.

values.da: Andre husstande bestående af flere familier

icd10.name: ICD-10 (WHO form)
icd10.description: Diagnosis codes in the plain WHO form, letter followed by digits, with no prefix: E119 rather than DE119. This is what the cause-of-death registers hold. The patient registers hold the D-prefixed SKS form instead, which is `icd10_sks`.
icd10.note: Do not strip a leading D from these codes. The habit comes from LPR, where the D is really there, and applying it here removes the first character of a real code: E119 becomes 119, which matches nothing and raises no error. The danger is worst where a code genuinely begins with D. ICD-10 chapter D covers in-situ and benign neoplasms, so D46 is myelodysplastic syndrome, a whole code. Strip its "prefix" and you get 46, which looks like a code and is not one.

icd10_sks.name: ICD-10, Danish SKS form (D-prefixed)
icd10_sks.description: Diagnosis codes as the patient registers store them: the WHO code with the letter D in front, so WHO's E11 appears as DE11. This is an LPR form, not a property of Danish ICD-10 in general. The cause-of-death registers store the plain WHO code and use `icd10` instead.
icd10_sks.note: The D prefix is a Danish addition, not part of the WHO code. Matching WHO codes directly against LPR without allowing for it returns nothing. Do not carry the habit across to the cause-of-death registers: they hold the plain code, so stripping a D there removes the first real character instead.

icd8.name: ICD-8
icd8.description: Diagnosis codes as the patient registers stored them before 1994. Pure digits, no letter and no decimal point, so 446.30 is written 44630. Nothing about them looks like ICD-10, which is what makes them easy to mistake for a broken column rather than a different classification.
icd8.note: A study whose period starts before 1994 is reading two classifications out of one column. ICD-10 codes match nothing in the early years, and the usual substr(c_diag, 2, 4) returns a meaningless fragment of an ICD-8 code rather than failing, so nothing tells you it went wrong.
icd8.source_name: Retired classification, no current DST page

ie_type.name: IE-type (herkomst)
ie_type.description: Whether a person is of Danish origin, an immigrant or a descendant.
ie_type.note: DST's current high-quality page for IE_TYPE states that the variable has no value set. The codes here come from the older TIMES3 archive page, which does publish them.

indm.name: Indlaeggelsesmaade (LPR2 c_indm)
indm.description: Whether the contact was acute or planned. Three codes, one of which was discontinued.
indm.note: From 2014 this is what separates an emergency-room visit from an ordinary outpatient one, because `c_pattype` code `3` was discontinued and both arrive as `2`. Code `9` (Uoplyst) stops at the end of 2003, so a missing value after that is genuinely missing rather than coded as unknown.

indud_kode.name: Indud_kode (migration direction)
indud_kode.description: Whether a migration event is an immigration or an emigration.
indud_kode.note: Use `U` for censoring at emigration. People who never emigrated have no `U` event at all, so they are simply absent rather than carrying a missing date. Two caveats from the guide: CPR only has complete immigration and emigration data from 1971, so someone who immigrated before that has no event and looks resident since birth; and a move to Greenland is a status of its own in CPR rather than an emigration. Confirm the values on your own delivery.

koen.name: Køn (sex)
koen.description: Sex as coded in BEF. Small enumerated set.
koen.note: DST's classification KOEN_V1_1980 also defines `9` for not stated, which a delivery may not contain but a value set should. Sex is taken from the tenth digit of the CPR number: even is female, odd is male.

kom.name: Kommunekode (municipality code)
kom.description: Municipality of residence. Three-digit codes. 98 municipalities since the 2007 reform, which replaced the previous 271. Christiansø (411) is not under a municipality but administered directly by the state.
kom.note: These codes are valid from 1 January 2007. A study reaching further back needs the pre-reform classification, where the same number can mean a different municipality - confirmed for two reused codes against a current-only DST source: 707 is Norddjurs today, not its pre-2007 meaning, and likewise 849 is Jammerbugt. `lookup:` below covers only this post-2007 set (99 entries), not the full 278-code `values_from` file. Christiansø (411) is included in `lookup:` even though it is not a municipality (see description above): it is a real value a `kom` column can hold, and DST's own current-only classification lists it as its own area code alongside the 98 municipalities. Excluding it would just move the "unhandled code" problem this fix is meant to solve onto that one value.

kont_type.name: Contact type (LPR3 kont_type)
kont_type.description: The LPR3 contact type. Documented as SKS codes rather than the single digits LPR2 used, so the values look nothing like LPR2's c_pattype and cannot be mapped across one to one. In practice the column holds BOTH, and which one a row holds is decided by `lprindberetningssystem`, not by the year: rows reported through LPR3 carry the SKS codes, rows reported through MiniPAS carry LPR2 patient types (`0` and `2`, see the `pattype` code system). Both were present as late as 2024 in a delivery checked in 2026.
kont_type.note: `ALCA00` means physical attendance, which is the closest LPR3 gets to LPR2's inpatient flag. It marks attendance, not admission, so a study that treats it as "was admitted" will include outpatient visits. Check what your own delivery holds before filtering: single digits and SKS codes have been seen side by side in the same year, so `kont_type == "ALCA00"` can silently drop rows that are the same kind of contact recorded in the other form. Cross-tabulate it against `lprindberetningssystem` first. MiniPAS was the route private providers reported through, so the two forms are not only two notations, they are also two different parts of the health service.

nace_db07.name: DB07 brancheklassifikation (industry, NACE Rev.2)
nace_db07.description: Danish industry classification DB07, aligned with EU NACE Rev.2, current from 2007-2008. Hierarchical: level 1 is a small set of broad sections, level 2 the detailed code.
nace_db07.note: Two things to check before using this as a lookup. First, format: this file writes the detailed code with dots (01.11.00); nace_db07 and nace_db07_13 hold it without them (011100). Second, coverage: checked against nace_db07's own value list on DST's high-quality variable page, only 490 of its 743 distinct codes match this file's 738 level-2 codes even after stripping dots. As with DISCO-08 (see disco08.yaml), the industry code for a given person-year can be sourced from more than one register, so a code absent from this CSV is not necessarily an error.

nace_old.name: NACE brancheklassifikation, foer DB07 (2007)
nace_old.description: Industry of a person's main employment, before the 2007-2008 switch to DB07/NACE Rev.2. No published value list has been found for this revision, only its successor's.
nace_old.note: Do not read a code here against DB07/NACE Rev.2's published list (nace_db07.yaml): the 2007-2008 revision changed the code structure, and a code that means one industry under DB07 is not guaranteed to mean the same thing, or to exist at all, under this older scheme.

nystgr.name: Stillingsgruppering, 1980-1995 (AKM)
nystgr.description: A four-digit occupation/position grouping used before DISCO. The first digit marks the broad labour-market position (self-employed, employee, out of the labour force and so on), the rest the specific occupation within it.
nystgr.note: Retired in 1995 and replaced by DISCO. A code's meaning can shift within the window a study covers: DST's own page notes that code 5100 changed meaning in 1992 (the group it now names used code 5500 before that year), so a series spanning 1992 needs the year-by-year note on the source page, not just the current label.

omfang.name: Omfang af skattepligt (AKM/Indkomst)
omfang.description: How fully a person's tax and income data cover the year: fully liable both 1 January and 31 December, moved during the year, died during the year, a child with no income, or one of a few edge cases the tax and settlement registers cannot reconcile. Not a demographic fact about the person, an administrative fact about how complete their income record is.
omfang.note: Code 2 changed meaning at the 2002 boundary: before 2002 (and again 2002-2009) it also absorbed children under 15 with no income or wealth, a group that codes 0 and 4 cover separately in other years. Code 5 (died, not settled) only exists from 2002; before that, a death with no settled income was coded 2 instead. DST's own publications and statistikbanktabeller are restricted to omfang=1: an analysis that does not filter on it silently includes partial-year residents, the newly dead, and unsettled records alongside ordinary full-year taxpayers.

oprart.name: Procedureart (LPR2 c_oprart)
oprart.description: What role a procedure code plays on the contact: the main one, a sub-procedure or an add-on code.
oprart.note: Counting rows in the procedure table counts add-on codes and sub-procedures as procedures. If you want one row per operation, filter to `V` or `P` first. All four codes run from 1996 with no breaks.

values.en: Main procedure of the completed contact

pattype.name: Patienttype (LPR2 c_pattype)
pattype.description: The patient's administrative relationship to the hospital. LPR2 only: LPR3 has no equivalent, and the type has to be derived from contact duration plus an acute marker.
pattype.note: There are four codes, not six, and three of them changed meaning. Code `1` was Dagpatient until 1986 and Deldoegnspatient from 1987, and then stops entirely at the end of 2001. Code `2` was Natpatient until 1986 and Ambulant from 1987. Code `0` was Heldoegnspatient until 2001 and Indlagt patient from 2002. The register only started using `1`, `2` and `3` in 1994, so before that essentially every contact is `0`. Code `3` was discontinued at the end of 2013, and from 2014 an emergency-room visit arrives as `2` with an acute admission mode in `c_indm`. Reading `2` as outpatient across the whole register therefore mislabels night patients before 1987 and emergency visits after 2013.

plads.name: Familiestatus (plads i familien)
plads.description: A person's position in the family.

reg.name: Region
reg.description: Region of residence. The five regions created by the 2007 municipal reform, plus a code for unknown.
reg.note: Do not confuse these with AMT, the pre-2007 counties, which has 16 codes in the ranges 11-14, 21-24, 31-37 and 88. Different geography, different era.

sex_lpr.name: Koen in LPR2 (c_sex)
sex_lpr.description: Sex as recorded on a hospital contact. Not the same coding as BEF's `koen`, and not the same coding across the register's own lifetime.
sex_lpr.note: The coding changed at the start of 2005: `1`/`2` until the end of 2004, `M`/`K` from 2005. A study spanning that year that filters on `c_sex == "2"` keeps only the women seen before 2005 and silently drops the rest, with no error and no empty result to warn you. Take sex from BEF instead, where it is `koen` coded `1`/`2` throughout, unless you specifically need what the hospital recorded.

sks.name: SKS procedure codes
sks.description: Sundhedsvaesenets Klassifikations System. The procedure branch of the same classification that supplies diagnosis codes, used in LPR_SKSOPR and LPR_SKSUBE. Surgical procedures sit under K, examinations and other non-surgical procedures under the remaining letters.
sks.note: The codes are hierarchical, so a prefix match selects a whole branch. That also makes it easy to select more than you meant: check how many characters your intended group actually needs before filtering with starts_with().

socio13.name: Socioøkonomisk klassifikation (SOCIO13)
socio13.description: Socioeconomic position: what a person mainly lived on during the year. The codes are hierarchical, so the first digit is the broad group and the third the detail.
socio13.note: Two codes are easy to misread. `410` is **Andre** (other), not unemployed: the unemployed are `210`. And `420` is **children under 15**, a known category rather than a missing value, so it appearing in an adult cohort means the index date is wrong rather than the data being incomplete.

akm.name: Arbejdsklassifikationsmodulet (labour classification module)
akm.description: One record per person per year with their socioeconomic classification: employed, self-employed, student, unemployed, pensioner, outside the labour market.
akm.grain: one row per person per period

bef.name: Befolkningen (population register)
bef.description: Status register with one snapshot per person per reference time point. Delivered quarterly since 2008 (March, June, September, December); December only before that, so the cadence is not constant across the coverage.
bef.grain: one row per person per period

cancer.name: Cancerregisteret
cancer.description: One row per incident cancer diagnosis: a person appears once per tumour, not once in total. Running since 1943, which makes it one of the longest continuous cancer registries in the world.

dod.name: Døde i Danmark (deaths in Denmark)
dod.description: One row per deceased person. This is the register to use for date of death, and it covers the whole period on its own.

dodsaars.name: Dødsårssagsregistret
dodsaars.description: Cause of death for 1970-2001. Closed. It also carries a date of death, which is why it is so often used for censoring, but that use is a mistake for any study running past 2001.

dodsaarsager.name: Dødsårsagsregister (2022-)
dodsaarsager.description: Cause of death from 2022. The current register, and the third naming scheme the chain has used.

dodsaasg.name: Dødsårsagsregister (2002-2022)
dodsaasg.description: Cause of death for 2002-2022. Closed. Takes over from DODSAARS and is itself replaced by DODSAARSAGER.

faik.name: Familieindkomster (family income)
faik.description: Household income per year, keyed on the household rather than the person. Reaching it from a person means going through BEF for the familie_id.
faik.grain: one row per family per year

lab_dm_forsker.name: Laboratoriedatabasens Forskertabel
lab_dm_forsker.description: One row per laboratory result attached to a request: a blood or other sample, its analyte code, the result and its unit. Very large - well over a billion rows - so filter before collecting.

lmdb.name: Lægemiddeldatabasen (prescription register)
lmdb.description: One row per dispensed prescription, so the same person appears many times. Covers prescriptions dispensed at community pharmacies.

lpr_a_diagnose.name: Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - diagnoseoplysning
lpr_a_diagnose.description: One row per diagnosis on a contact. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_a_kontakt on dw_ek_kontakt to reach the person.
lpr_a_diagnose.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_a_kontakt.name: Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - kontaktoplysninger
lpr_a_kontakt.description: One row per hospital contact. Carries pnr, so the diagnosis and procedure tables reach the person through it. DST gives the coverage as 2017-2025: the table reaches back before the March 2019 LPR3 boundary because outpatient contacts already held in LPR2 were folded into it.

lpr_a_procregistrering.name: Landspatientregistret (LPR3) - procedureregistreringer
lpr_a_procregistrering.description: One row per procedure registration. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_a_kontakt on dw_ek_kontakt, exactly as the diagnosis table does.
lpr_a_procregistrering.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_adm.name: Landspatientregistret - administrative oplysninger
lpr_adm.description: One row per hospital contact. This is the only LPR2 dataset that carries pnr, so every other one reaches the person through it.

lpr_diag.name: Landspatientregistret - diagnoser
lpr_diag.description: One row per diagnosis on a contact, so a contact can have several. Carries no pnr: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person.
lpr_diag.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_sksopr.name: Landspatientregistret - operationer
lpr_sksopr.description: One row per surgical procedure. Carries no pnr and no admission date: join to lpr_adm on recnum to reach the person.
lpr_sksopr.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

lpr_sksube.name: Landspatientregistret - undersoegelser og behandlinger
lpr_sksube.description: One row per examination or treatment. Structured exactly like LPR_SKSOPR, and joined to lpr_adm on recnum in the same way.
lpr_sksube.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

mfr.name: MFR - Levendefoedte fra det medicinske foedselsregister
mfr.description: One row per live birth, carrying both the mother and the child. A mother appears once per birth, so the register is keyed on the child rather than the person. DST cuts several other datasets from the same underlying register (stillbirths, pregnancy complications, home births and more); this is only the live-births one.

sssy.name: Sygesikring (6-cifret)
sssy.description: The continuation of SYSI: fees settled for primary-care activity. Same shape, a few different columns. Both registers report 2005, so a study spanning the handover has to pick one source for that year or it will double-count.

sysi.name: Sygesikring (6-cifret)
sysi.description: Fees settled for primary-care activity: general practice, practising specialists, dentists, physiotherapists and so on. One row per settled service group, not one row per visit.

t_psyk_adm.name: Landspatientregistret psykiatri - administrative oplysninger
t_psyk_adm.description: One row per psychiatric hospital contact, up to March 2019. The psychiatric counterpart of lpr_adm, and separate from it: a study covering both somatic and psychiatric care has to read both registers and stack them.

t_psyk_diag.name: Landspatientregistret psykiatri - diagnoser
t_psyk_diag.description: One row per diagnosis on a psychiatric contact. Carries no person identifier: join to t_psyk_adm to reach the person.
t_psyk_diag.grain: several rows per record in the parent table

udda.name: Uddannelser (BUE) (education register)
udda.description: One record per person per year, updated when the education changes. Holds the code for the education a person completed, not its level.
udda.grain: one row per person per period

vnds.name: Historiske vandringer (historical migrations)
vnds.description: One row per migration event per person: an immigration to or an emigration from Denmark, with the date it happened. Holds only events, so a person born in Denmark who never left has no rows at all - absence is the normal case, not missing data. Known to contain duplicates, which is why DST replaced it. Closed by DST and replaced by three registers: VNDS_IND and VNDS_UD from 2005, and VNDS_HIST for 1973-2004. VNDS itself runs to 2024, so its coverage overlaps both successors for 2005-2024. Closed by DST in February 2026 and split into VNDS_IND, VNDS_UD and VNDS_HIST. Still documented as a current register because deliveries made before the split contain only this one, which is the case for many projects.
vnds.overlap_note: Coverage overlaps the successors for 2005-2024, but they must not be combined. DST states that migration data over the years came from different sources and that this produced a number of duplicates, and that freezing the earliest data in a historical register reduces the problem. The three successors are therefore a correction of this register, not a reorganisation of it. Use either VNDS on its own, accepting the duplicates it is known to contain, or VNDS_HIST together with VNDS_IND and VNDS_UD - never a mixture.

vnds_hist.name: Historiske vandringer fra 1973 til 2004
vnds_hist.description: One row per migration event per person for 1973-2004. Frozen: DST marks it as closed, and it is not updated.

vnds_ind.name: Indvandringer (immigrations)
vnds_ind.description: One row per immigration from 2005 onwards, with the person's demographics as at the event.

vnds_ud.name: Udvandringer (emigrations)
vnds_ud.description: One row per emigration from 2005 onwards, with the person's demographics as at the event.
